description: The user's own standing list of tools, materials, references and software — the things they OWN or rely on, independent of any one job. Projects draw from it; it outlives them. Import FORTY-FIRST (no dependencies)
notes: WHY THIS IS NOT project_items (37) OR project_tools (40). Those two are per-job rows: 'this kitchen needs 4 litres of primer', 'this job needs a hired SDS drill for 2 days'. They are created for a project and die with it. This table is the standing kit — the drill you already own, the Figma seat you pay for, the wiring diagram you keep going back to. Without it you retype 'Cordless drill' into every project and the app can never answer 'what do I actually have'.

The relationship is COPY, not link: adding a toolkit item to a project creates a project_item or project_tool row prefilled from it. That is deliberate. A job's row records what that job needed at that time — quantity, cost, supplier — and editing the catalogue afterwards must not rewrite the history of a finished job.

kind decides which of the money fields mean anything. tool/equipment: unit_cost is what it cost you, quantity is usually 1. material: quantity and unit_cost are the ones that matter, and it is consumed. software: unit_cost is a recurring seat, so read it with renews_on. reference: no money at all.

status is about availability, not condition. have = in hand, usable now. need = do not have it and a job wants it. ordered = paid for, not arrived. loaned_out = yours, someone else has it. broken = yours, cannot be used. 'need' and 'broken' are what a shopping list is built from.

location is free text ('garage shelf', 'van', 'top drawer') because the next answer is never in a list written in advance. It is the single most useful field for a physical item and the one people most regret not filling in.

linked_habit_ids is a comma-separated list of habit-library slugs, matching the depends_on convention on user_tasks. It connects the kit to the habit that needs it — a barbell to Back squat — so 'what do I need to start this habit' has an answer.
user_id is plain text holding String(user.id). Users live in Xano; see 00-import-order.md.

FORGEABLE, like every table here: the Baserow token ships in the client bundle. This is a personal list, so the blast radius is one user's own kit, but do not build anything that trusts unit_cost as a financial record.

user_id.description: Xano user id as a string

icon.description: Emoji shown in lists. Falls back to a per-kind default.

quantity.description: How many you have. Fractional for materials sold by length or weight.

unit_cost.description: Cost of ONE. Baserow rejects a row whose value exceeds the field's decimal places, so this is 2dp, not 0.

supplier.description: Who you get it from. Free text.

url.description: Product page, doc, or the software itself

purchased_on.description: Date only — no time. When you got it.

renews_on.description: Software only: when the subscription next bills.

linked_habit_ids.description: Comma-separated habit-library slugs this kit supports

note.description: Anything that will not fit above: model number, which charger, who borrowed it

archived.description: Kept for history, hidden from the list. Sold or thrown out.
